name: Harpy
summary: Across Kalimdor and Alterac's high passes, Harpies foul their roosts and hunt travelers. Their shrieks and storm magic are feared, while night elf tales link them to Azshara's cursed betrayers. Their true origins remain uncertain.

sections.title: Winged Scourge of Kalimdor
sections.body: Harpies spread from the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains across Kalimdor. Their heads and upper bodies resemble night elf women, with broad feathered wings and wicked talons. Age makes their elven faces more striking, but their nature is savage. They terrorize Durotar's arid canyons, Teldrassil's sacred boughs, and the heights of Mulgore. Around their roosts, they despoil plant and animal life, leaving the picked-clean bones of their prey.

sections.title: Avian Lineage and Dark Nature
sections.body: Night elf tales say harpies began as handmaidens who betrayed Queen Azshara and were cursed before the Great Sundering. Their true origins remain uncertain. Today, ruthless matriarchies rule the harpies. Those who seek command betray, slaughter, and torment their rivals to hold it.

sections.title: Tempest Magic and Wicked Habits
sections.body: Harpies tear flesh with razor-sharp claws and wield dangerous wind and lightning magic. From above, their shrieking gales batter their foes. Cunning hunters, they can speak and sometimes trade scavenged oddities with subterranean creatures such as kobolds for bright gems and shiny trinkets. Their elven forms can beguile unwary explorers, but their kiss is venomous and swiftly brings a violent, wasting fever.

faq.q: Where do harpies originally come from?
faq.answer: Harpies first roosted among the jagged peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains in central Kalimdor. From there, they spread to Teldrassil, the Barrens, Durotar, Mulgore, Feralas, and the Thousand Needles. They also crossed the Great Sea to Alterac Valley's snowy crags.

faq.q: Are harpies actually related to night elves?
faq.answer: Kalimdor folklore says harpies were night elf women cursed for betraying Queen Azshara. Their elven features fit the tale, but no one knows whether it is true.

faq.q: Why are harpy nests so infamous?
faq.answer: Harpies foul the land around their nests, leaving stench-ridden middens of trampled foliage and noxious waste. They also leave butchered bones and remnants of travelers and beasts dragged from nearby trails.

faq.q: How do harpy covens choose their leaders?
faq.answer: Harpies fiercely contest leadership. To claim and hold command as queen or matriarch, one must prove more ruthless than her roost-mates through betrayal, murder, and relentless cruelty toward enemies and rivals.

faq.q: What powers and combat tactics do harpies use?
faq.answer: Harpies attack with crude weapons or razor-sharp talons, often diving from above. Their spellcasters wield storm magic, striking with crackling lightning, swirling gusts of wind, and shrill, disorienting shrieks.

faq.q: Is it true that a harpy's kiss is dangerous?
faq.answer: Yes. A harpy's kiss is toxic. Travelers beguiled by her elven features risk potent poison if they let her close, and it swiftly brings a sudden, debilitating fever.

angles.text: Harpies resemble night elf women, yet they despoil the sacred boughs around Teldrassil's Oracle Glade.
The Windfury harpies of Mulgore and the Screeching brood of Thousand Needles have plagued tauren caravans and blighted the plains for generations. The tribes revile them as enemies.
Dustwind harpies roost in Drygulch Ravine and Razorwind Canyon, where they menace supply routes between Sen'jin Village, Razor Hill, and Orgrimmar. Constant armed patrols are needed.
Harpies scorn nature's balance and foul the wilderness with tempest magic and filthy nests.
